rows.en:
At that instant there was a sound like thunder, and a pale blue light began to shine in midair.
The girls held their breath and watched what was happening.
And then the demon appeared.
Slowly, slowly, a demon with a horrifying face emerged from the pale blue light.{p}

The girls regretted what they had done.
(Maybe we've done something terrible...)
That was what Sawada thought.
But there was no turning back.
She had to see it through until she sent the demon back.
She went on with the incantation.
And just as she was about to say the final spell to send the demon back...{p}

"Eeeek!"
One of the girls tried to run and took a step out of the magic circle.
The instant she did, she was turned into chunks of flesh.
The other girls screamed.
Another girl tried to flee, stepped outside the circle, and in a flash she too became chunks of flesh.
Their terror had reached its peak.{p}What do you think they did after that?
They blamed Sawada
They tried hard to make the demon go away

"This is all your fault, Eri!"
Endo accused her.
And then Sawada and the others got into an argument.
"You... you're the ones who wanted this!"
"We never told you to summon a demon like this!"
"You know a little more than us, so it went to your head!"
"That's right, it's Eri's fault!"
All of them turned on Sawada.
Sawada, who at first had kept her head down in silence, suddenly said this.{p}

"Who do you think you are...?
You can all just go and die.
I command you: kill them!"
Sawada said it holding the book up high.

Though they had never left the magic circle, the girls who had bad-mouthed her turned into chunks of flesh in an instant. Then the demon vanished into the pale blue light.
Left behind were a few girls and Sawada, and the scattered chunks of flesh had vanished without a trace.{p}

Some people say the demon devoured her in exchange for her wish, but nobody knows the truth.
That was when it started.
Strange, inexplicable spirits began appearing at that spot.

They say it's the grudge of the girls the demon killed that night.
Maybe the girls killed by the demon couldn't rest in peace and stayed at that spot. But since the exorcism held later, they seem to have gone quiet.
How do I know all this, you ask?
Obviously, because a girl who survived that night told someone.
It's probably better that I don't tell you what became of that girl.
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}

Sawada started searching the book for a way to drive the demon away.
"Someone... one of us has to be sacrificed."
When Sawada said that, the girls looked at each other.
"Eri, you're the one who summoned it.
You said it would be fine, so..."
She didn't say the last words.
But everyone knew what she meant.
All their eyes fixed on Sawada.
"I never thought such a powerful demon would come out!"
Nobody would say a word.
They all knew it: Sawada was the only one who knew how.
And to get Sawada to go through with it, one of them would have to be the sacrifice.
"Let's draw lots.
But Eri, you show everyone how to do it before you draw."
"All right..."{p}

Sawada showed them the page where the method was written, then set the book down on the ground.
Then she made lots out of fallen leaves from the ground.{p}At that moment, where do you think Sawada drew her lot from?
From the right side
Somewhere in the middle
From the left side

The lot fell to Sawada.
A girl who had drawn a blank snatched up the book lying on the ground with frightening speed and clutched it to her chest.
"All right, let's do this!"
But when she read the book, she suddenly crouched down on the ground.
"What?! It won't work unless it's the person who summoned it!"
With that, she burst into tears.{p}

Sawada began to laugh eerily, and said this.
"That's right. I don't have to be the sacrifice.
Heh heh heh.
Now, decide who's going to be the sacrifice."
A girl who ran away in sheer terror was turned into chunks of flesh too.
"Well? Who's it going to be?"
"Let's pick her."
"Why me?! What did I ever do?!"
After arguing it out, the girls decided who would be sacrificed.
She wept and refused, but no one would listen.{p}

When the incantation ended, the girl's body rose into the air and moved toward the demon.
An explosion roared all around, and every girl watching fainted.{p}

The next morning, the teachers found them.
But they say their faces were too hideous to look at twice.
No one knows why.
And then, they say, every one of them killed herself at the very spot where they had held the ritual.
They say their spirits, unable to rest, are still at that spot today.
That's why accidents kept happening there.
According to the infirmary records, most of the students who had accidents were girls, especially pretty ones.
Now, maybe because the exorcism worked, there are no accidents.
But anyone who passes near there should be careful, especially girls who are confident about their looks.
There's no telling when the accidents will start again.
That's the end of my story.
Next person, please.{p}

Sawada drew.
"Mine's a blank."
The other girls drew their lots one after another.
After drawing, some peeked at theirs in secret, and some were too scared to look.
And then there were two leaves left.
Endo said, almost in a murmur,
"So the one that's left over is mine."
Then the last girl drew.
"Who got it?"
Sawada said it with an eerie laugh.
Endo looked at the leaf that was left.{p}

"I-it's me."
"So it's you."
Everyone looked at Endo, relieved.
"All right, I'm starting."
Sawada began to chant the incantation.
And when she finished...
With a crash of thunder, Endo's body rose into the air and moved toward the demon.
"If I remember right, you grant wishes, don't you?"
"............yes............"
The demon said it in a voice that made the ground shake.
"Then give those girls ugly faces and miserable lives."
Endo flung the words out.
"............yes............"
"What are you saying? You're the one who drew the short straw!"
Sawada said, her voice shaking.
"That's right. You all get to keep your lives, so what's the problem?"
Endo said it in a bright, and eerie, voice.
The girls fainted.{p}

Then the face in the mirror grew uglier and uglier.
Sawada screamed in terror and fainted.{p}

They say the girls are still in the hospital even now.
Even if you go to the hospital, you won't find the ugly face Sawada says she saw.
What on earth was that ugly face Sawada saw?
They say she's the only one who talks about it; nobody else ever saw anything like it.
But whenever Sawada looks into a mirror, she sees it, they say. That ugly face.
That's the end of my story.
Next person, please.{p}

Sawada drew.
"Mine's a blank."
The other girls drew their lots one after another.
"Noooo! Why me?!
I only tagged along!"
The lot fell to a girl who'd been standing off in the corner.
She backed away and tried to run.
"Hold it!"
The girls near her pinned her arms behind her and, so they say, dragged her over to Sawada.{p}
"Come on, Sawada, do it."

The girl screamed and wailed.
But with so many girls holding her down, she couldn't move.
"Please, forgive meee!"
Sawada began to chant the incantation.{p}

The girl's body lifted lightly into the air and flew toward the demon.
And when she reached the demon, with a sound like an explosion, both the demon and the girl vanished. The girls fainted where they stood.{p}

The next morning, a teacher found them.
The teacher asked them what had happened, but every one of them kept her mouth shut.
In the end, the missing student was never found, and it was written off as a runaway case.
From then on, an earthbound spirit started appearing here.
They say those girls went on attending this school afterward.
And that they lived calmly, as if nothing had ever happened.
That's the end of my story.
Next person, please.{p}

Surprised?
That's right, it's the incinerator.
I think the teachers probably didn't take it seriously.
Otherwise they'd never have built something like an incinerator there, would they?
So the accidents went on even after the incinerator was built.
But the school just sat on its hands and couldn't do anything about it.
Officially, they didn't warn the students about anything, especially not about the incinerator.
Then one day, a member of the biology committee threw a dead rabbit into the incinerator and burned it.{p}

A solution had been found.
The teachers talked it over and decided to offer an animal carcass as a sacrifice every week. But about half a year later...
The school year changed, and new teachers arrived.
Among them was a teacher fresh out of college named Koji Someya.
One day, Mr. Someya's turn came up to put the sacrifice into the incinerator.
Even though the accidents had stopped, no teacher was happy to go every week.
So they had decided to take turns.
"Mr. Someya, you may think this is ridiculous, but.................."
With that, a senior teacher explained how it had all come about.
"Well then, I'm counting on you."
When that teacher left, Mr. Someya reluctantly headed for the incinerator.{p}

"This is so damn stupid.
It's creepy.
Just my luck that my first school turns out to be a place like this."
When he went around behind the school building, he could see the incinerator.{p}

"There it is. Let's get this over with."
And he headed toward the incinerator.
A little way on, he saw some students fighting.
"What do you think you're doing?!"
When Mr. Someya shouted, the two students ran off.
He forgot all about the sacrifice and chased after them.
When he caught up with the two students, he gave them a thorough chewing out.{p}

The next day, when he got to school, the faculty room was in an uproar.
"What's going on?"
"Early this morning, a student was badly hurt near the incinerator."
"Mr. Someya, you did the sacrifice properly, didn't you?"
"Huh? Y-yes."
Mr. Someya ended up telling a lie without thinking.

"I see.
Maybe something on that level isn't enough to calm the spirit anymore."
The teachers were discussing what to do from now on.
(Damn it. I never thought something like this would really happen.)
He regretted it.{p}What do you think Mr. Someya did after that?
He honestly owned up
He kept up the lie

He told the truth.
And after school, he went to the incinerator to offer the sacrifice once more.{p}

The sacrifice he had failed to offer yesterday was in a corner of the school building, as if hidden away.
"I have to offer the sacrifice, quickly."
The sun had set, and it had grown quite dark.
When he reached the incinerator, he opened the door and threw in the animal carcass.
"That should do it."
And just as he took out his lighter to light it...{p}

From the darkness all around, dozens of yellow eyes were staring at him.
"Uh... uh... aaagh!"
The teacher was so startled he dropped the lighter.

It was an oil lighter, so it kept burning there on the ground.
The teacher braced himself, sure the monsters would attack, but they only prowled around at a distance and didn't come at him.
This went on for a while, until the lighter ran out of oil.

It was the moment the flame went out with a puff.
The monsters suddenly attacked.
They tore the flesh from the teacher's arms and legs with their teeth.
Just when he thought this was the end, he saw a box of matches lying on the ground.
He desperately grabbed it and struck a match.
Then the monsters suddenly stopped attacking.{p}

The teacher kept striking match after match.
And then he was down to the last one.
(This is it. I'm finished.)
That's what he thought.
Then he took one last gamble.
He lit the last match and threw it into the incinerator.{p}

Did you know? You've never seen the fire in that incinerator go out, have you?
This is actually the reason.
It's a kind of charm against evil, you could say.
If you ever see that incinerator with its fire out, I think you'd better not go near it.
There's no telling what might happen.
That's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}

Mr. Someya decided to keep up the lie.
(I finally made it as a teacher. If I cause trouble now...)
When he thought that, he just couldn't bring himself to say it.
He went through the day as if he knew nothing.
After talking it over, the teachers decided to hold an exorcism.{p}

The next Sunday, they called in the head priest of a nearby temple, nearly all the teachers gathered, and the exorcism began.
Mr. Someya prayed desperately.
And for a while, nothing happened.
The animal sacrifices were resumed, and were carried out once a week.{p}

About three months later, Mr. Someya's turn came around.
(I hope nothing happens...)
Mr. Someya thought about telling the truth and asking someone to take his place, but he just couldn't bring himself to do it.
(I have to go.)
Telling himself that, Mr. Someya headed for the incinerator.{p}

When he reached the incinerator, Mr. Someya hurriedly opened the door and threw the sacrifice inside.
Then he took out his lighter and, lighter in hand, reached into the incinerator.

Mr. Someya screamed and yanked his hand back out.
Several of his fingers had been bitten off.
And when he turned to flee, he saw countless rat-like animals covering the ground.
His legs gave out, and he collapsed onto the ground.{p}

And then the rat-like animals attacked.
They swarmed over him until he was buried.{p}

A while later, when another teacher happened by, he was barely breathing.
They say he confessed everything that had happened to that teacher, and then breathed his last.
Ever since then, they say, the animal carcass sacrifices are never skipped.
They might even be doing it today.
If you feel like it, why not go have a look later?
In reporting, it's important to confirm things with your own eyes, after all.
That's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}

Did you know this story?
There's a flower bed behind the gym, isn't there?
That's actually the place.
A teacher from back then turned it into a flower bed because so many accidents happened there.
But making it a flower bed didn't mean the accidents stopped right away.
The accidents never stopped among the gardening committee students who tended the flower bed.
And the gardening committee students gradually stopped going near it.{p}

The flower bed fell into ruin and was overrun with weeds.
One day, a new first-year girl on the gardening committee, who didn't know what had happened there, pulled the weeds and planted sunflowers.
But she had an accident too, and had to give up partway.
That summer there was a long stretch without rain, yet the sunflowers grew steadily.
Then one day, one of the chickens the school kept got loose.
It was a dull, overcast day; it had already gotten quite dark, and only a few students were still around.{p}

Yamabe from the animal-care committee was chasing the chicken for all he was worth when he passed in front of the flower bed.
(Oh crap, this is THAT flower bed.)
Thinking that, he stopped.
The chicken kept running, cutting right across in front of the flower bed.{p}

A sunflower stretched out, long and slithering, and bit the chicken.
And then it began to eat the chicken.
Yamabe was so terrified he couldn't even run.
When it had finished eating the chicken, the sunflower turned back into an ordinary sunflower.
All that was left were the chicken's feathers.{p}

That night, Yamabe was thinking about the sunflowers.
And he hit on the idea of luring his homeroom teacher, Mr. Saito, whom he had always hated, to the sunflower bed.

For a while, he watched for his chance.
"A person won't die from it, probably."
The teachers knew about that flower bed too.
If he just called Mr. Saito out there normally, he would never come.
Then his chance came.{p}

Mr. Saito was in a corner of the schoolyard, watching practice for the softball team he advised.
Seeing that, Yamabe said this to him.{p}

"Suzuki got hurt behind the school building. Please come with me."
However far the bad rumors about the flower bed had spread, nobody knew about the sunflowers.
If a student was hurt, he couldn't very well not go.
"Where...?"
"At that flower bed."
For an instant the teacher looked startled, but when he'd been told a student was hurt, he couldn't refuse because of some superstitious ghost story.{p}

Mr. Saito went up to the flower bed, steeled himself, and stepped inside it.
Yamabe watched, his heart swelling with anticipation.
"Where are they, Yamabe?"
And then the sunflowers began to move, just like that time.{p}
"GYAAAHH!"

"Heeelp meee!"
With a pitiful look on his face, the teacher begged Yamabe for help.
Yamabe looked at Mr. Saito and laughed under his breath.
"Heh... heh, heh heh."
He was satisfied that his plan had gone just as he wanted, and satisfied by Mr. Saito's pathetic state.
After a while, the screaming stopped.{p}

"Sir, are you all right?"
Yamabe got worried and called out, but there was no answer.
When he peered into the flower bed from a distance, all that was left there were scraps of his suit.
"They eat people too..."
From then on, he fed everyone he didn't like to the sunflowers, one after another.
But one time, he was watching someone he didn't like being eaten in the usual place...{p}

After it finished eating that victim, a sunflower stretched toward Yamabe.
Yamabe knew the sunflowers couldn't reach where he was standing.
So he just stood there, unbothered.
As Yamabe watched the sunflower, it closed in fast until it was right in front of him.{p}

Mr. Saito laughed eerily.
Yamabe turned around to run.
But sunflowers had gathered all around him.
He was surrounded by sunflowers wearing the faces of everyone he had fed to them.
Yamabe understood his fate.{p}

By the time a teacher happened to pass by, it was already too late.
After his death, they say something called an 'assassination diary' was found in his room.
Then summer ended, and the sunflowers withered.
They held an exorcism and got rid of the sunflowers.
After that, no sunflowers were ever planted in that bed again.
And they say the teachers take turns making sure it never goes without water.
Maybe that's why there are no accidents now.
Rumor has it that seeds from those sunflowers are still somewhere in this school.
I wonder if the earthbound spirit is with those sunflower seeds now.
You be careful too, {a}{f:,|,} when you plant sunflower seeds.
As for me, I've decided never to plant sunflower seeds for as long as I live.
Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's next?{p}
